questionText: According to the text, young people are ignoring their environmental responsibilities. Do you agree? Refer to the text in support of your answer. (Two points, about 50 words in total.)

sourceMaterial.label: Reading Comprehension 1
sourceMaterial.title: Reading Comprehension 1 — answer in English or Irish
sourceMaterial.attribution: SEC French 2026 Higher Level examination paper — © State Examinations Commission.
sourceMaterial.presentationNote: Read the original passage and return to this task. Answer in English or Irish.

schemeCitation: SEC French 2026 Higher Level marking scheme, pp.10; general rules p.4 — © State Examinations Commission.

taskRequirements: Answer in English or Irish.
Use the separate answer spaces where provided. Two or more answers on one line count as one answer. An extra subdivision is rewarded only if an earlier answer is cancelled.

Excess material: deduct 1 or 2 marks. All other errors together: deduct at most 1 mark per question or segment (inappropriate quotation, unnecessary manipulation, grammar in manipulation, required manipulation not attempted, or wrong answer language). The excess-material penalty may also apply.
Give 2 distinct points. Each earns at most 5 marks; do not score the same point twice.
answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree and/or disagree using the following points.
Any two of:
Agree:
• Most 18 to 35 year-olds fly at least once a year
• People aged 25 to 34 hold the record for being the most frequent flyers
• Young people chose to fly because it doesn’t cost much
• They prioritise cheap flights over their environmental impact
• Availing of cheap flights is more important to them
• Flying is more convenient and economical, e.g. travelling by train is 4 or 5 times more expensive than flying
• Flying saves time, e.g. Ophélie cares more about not wasting a single day of her annual holidays, if she takes the train it uses up two days
• They ignore their environmental responsibilities to look good on social media while travelling
• Their desire to travel the world surpasses their need to uphold environmental beliefs
• The relentless pressure from the marketing of cheap flights causes them to ignore the impact on the environment
Etc., etc.
Disagree:
• Even environmentalists choose flying because travelling by train is 4 or 5 times more expensive
• Alice states that she is ecologically conscious
• Léa takes measures to help the environment, e.g. she doesn’t eat much meat / she sorts her waste / she rarely buys new clothes
• Young people are deliberately targeted by the marketing of airline companies, advertising, social media to choose low-cost flights
• A generation has grown up with the aeroplane, it’s the norm for them
• They are torn between environmental responsibility and a desire to travel
• Mathilde has not flown in four years
• Mathilde favours one big, longer trip instead of multiple trips
• Immense pressure to travel, to do thousands of activities, to tick the box of trips seen on Instagram
• Some young people, like Mathilde, refuse to yield to social media pressure to travel frequently
Etc., etc.

questionText: In this extract, Jeanne’s search for a tenant seems to be difficult. Do you agree? Refer to the text in support of your answer. (Two points, about 50 words in total.)

sourceMaterial.label: Reading Comprehension 2
sourceMaterial.title: Reading Comprehension 2 — answer in English or Irish
sourceMaterial.attribution: SEC French 2026 Higher Level examination paper — © State Examinations Commission.
sourceMaterial.presentationNote: Read the original passage and return to this task. Answer in English or Irish.

schemeCitation: SEC French 2026 Higher Level marking scheme, pp.17; general rules p.4 — © State Examinations Commission.

taskRequirements: Answer in English or Irish.
Use the separate answer spaces where provided. Two or more answers on one line count as one answer. An extra subdivision is rewarded only if an earlier answer is cancelled.

Excess material: deduct 1 or 2 marks. All other errors together: deduct at most 1 mark per question or segment (inappropriate quotation, unnecessary manipulation, grammar in manipulation, required manipulation not attempted, or wrong answer language). The excess-material penalty may also apply.
Give 2 distinct points. Each earns at most 5 marks; do not score the same point twice.
answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree and / or disagree using the following points.
Any two of:
Agree:
• She has to write out ads to try to find a tenant
• She has to go to the local shops to ask if she can post an advert, e.g. bakery, hair salon
• A total stranger puts his hand on her shoulder in the street
• She has difficulty understanding a potential tenant when he speaks to her
• She wasn’t fully prepared for this search, e.g. when asked how much the rent was, she hadn’t yet thought about how much to charge
• Her expectations are too high – she is looking for a pay-slip and a reference
• She has to get guarantees from prospective tenants, e.g. pay-slip and reference from current landlord
• She must study Luc’s documents and the young lady’s before making her mind up
• She can’t decide between Luc and the young woman, she hesitates, she can’t say no directly
• She is torn between a sense of justice and empathy
Etc., etc.
Disagree:
• She only barely began to post adverts in local businesses when a potential tenant shows keen interest
• On the same day, in a short amount of time, two potential tenants are interested in her room- to-let
• Her prospective tenants seem like good people; Luc claiming to be serious, the young woman says she is reliable, discreet/private/quiet
• It is more difficult for the potential tenants who have to plead for accommodation
• She has a choice between two potential tenants; she gets to choose the one she prefers
• She’s savvy. She knows to ask for relevant documents.
Etc., etc.

questionText: Scouting has become attractive for young people in the 21st century. Do you agree? Refer to the text in support of your answer. (Two points, about 50 words in total.)

sourceMaterial.label: Reading Comprehension 1
sourceMaterial.title: Reading Comprehension 1 — answer in English or Irish
sourceMaterial.attribution: SEC French 2025 Higher Level examination paper — © State Examinations Commission.
sourceMaterial.presentationNote: Read the original passage and return to this task. Answer in English or Irish.

schemeCitation: SEC French 2025 Higher Level marking scheme, pp.9; general rules p.4 — © State Examinations Commission.

taskRequirements: Answer in English or Irish.
Use the separate answer spaces where provided. Two or more answers on one line count as one answer. An extra subdivision is rewarded only if an earlier answer is cancelled.

Excess material: deduct 1 or 2 marks. All other errors together: deduct at most 1 mark per question or segment (inappropriate quotation, unnecessary manipulation, grammar in manipulation, required manipulation not attempted, or wrong answer language). The excess-material penalty may also apply.
Give 2 distinct points. Each earns at most 5 marks; do not score the same point twice.
answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree and / or disagree using the following points.
Any two of:
Agree:
• Scouting is becoming increasingly popular / More and more people are turning to scouting
• People want to go back to nature and go back to community living
• It brings together lots of members and volunteers
• In the 21st century there is a boom in scout membership
• The growth in membership started in the 2010s
• Membership grew even more following the 1st Covid lockdown in 2020
• Between 2012 and 2022 membership nearly doubled (increasing from 75,000 to 130,000 members)
• There are currently long waiting lists to join, forcing parents to act fast to sign their child up
• It involves lots of planned activities in the wild, at weekends and during school holidays
• Activities include team sports, gatherings of young people, citizen and solidarity commitments
• They become empowered and responsible, by learning to live together in harmony
• Activities teach them to be independent, organised and resourceful
• The values acquired complement what they learn at school
• The increase in popularity of scouting comes from the attractiveness of prices of their camps, 200 euro for a fortnight at a camp
• Most camps take place in the countryside. Everyone loves them
• Scouting is all about happiness / pleasure / joy, through games, songs and adventures
• Scouts sing while doing the washing-up, packing their tents, preparing their meals, walking long distances
• Their ideals of respect and closeness to nature are expressed through singing
• Scouts love to express themselves through songs
Etc., etc.
Disagree:
• It’s difficult to join due to the long waiting list
• Scouting in France has had both highs and lows
• There is a contribution of 200 euro to take part in a scout camp
Etc., etc.

answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree or disagree using the following points.
Any two of:
Agree:
• During the weekend before schools closed, Marie‐Solène emailed the parents with some simple activities for the children
• Ronan suggested making some videos
• Marie‐Solène agreed to do the broadcasts on YouTube
• Ronan saw the potential of the broadcasts as a respite for parents
• They have adapted their home / room
• Ronan organised the setting up and the link with the producer in Limoges
• They involved the parents
• Marie‐Solène adapted a new approach having been told that she wasn’t allowing the children enough time to answer
• Her delight in the broadcasts came across on the screen
• She succeeded in getting the children actively involved
• The number taking part reached 9,600 in a few weeks
• Her enthusiasm inspired other teachers to get involved and to help.
Etc., etc.
Disagree:
• Marie‐Solène initially rejects the idea of making videos
• She didn’t realise she wasn’t giving the children enough time to answer
• She didn’t want to hear about the number of children getting involved
• She found it very tiring and stressful.
• Classes began quite late in the afternoon and were on only four days a week
• She found it difficult to have to deal with parents as well as children.
Etc., etc.

sourceMaterial.attribution: SEC French 2021 Higher Level examination paper — © State Examinations Commission.
sourceMaterial.presentationNote: Read the original passage and return to this task. Answer in English or Irish.

schemeCitation: SEC French 2021 Higher Level marking scheme, pp.13; general rules p.4 — © State Examinations Commission.

taskRequirements: Answer in English or Irish.
Use the separate answer spaces where provided. Two or more answers on one line count as one answer. An extra subdivision is rewarded only if an earlier answer is cancelled.

Excess material: deduct 1 or 2 marks. All other errors together: deduct at most 1 mark per question or segment (inappropriate quotation, unnecessary manipulation, grammar in manipulation, required manipulation not attempted, or wrong answer language). The excess-material penalty may also apply.
Give 2 distinct points. Each earns at most 5 marks; do not score the same point twice.
answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree or disagree using the following points.
Any two of:
Agree:
• Dr Marnet’s wife is hospitable and invites Alex in to have some lemonade
• Conversation flows easily between them
• She shows a keen interest in his wheelchair
• She offers him advice on choosing a new wheelchair
• She shows Alex what you can do with a good wheelchair
• She greatly encourages him
• Both are independent
• Alex has a taste for adventure and wants to travel
• He has a positive attitude and doesn’t mind where he goes first
• He wants to see the world
• He believes it will be easier if Fabio and he travel together
• He wants to look for casual jobs to finance his travels
• He thinks this could be a fantastic project
• She approves of his plan, but points out the need for planning and organisation
• She offers help with getting grants / sponsorship
• Businesses would be prepared to help finance his travels
• She defends Alex when her husband is less than enthusiastic
• She smiles with satisfaction when Alex announces his plan to Dr Marnet
• She is in a wheelchair herself, so understands him better
• Because she is a wheelchair user, Alex feels that she will be more in tune with him
• The fact that two wheelchair users are portrayed in the text is in itself positive.
Etc., etc.
Disagree:
• Alex’s wheelchair is old and Dr Marnet’s wife is very negative about it
• His plans are vague
• She tells him travelling will require a lot of planning / a year’s planning
• He admits his idea was stupid
• She appears cautious about his plans.
• Alex feels he has to travel with another person who has a disability.
Etc., etc.

• She is resourceful in fast food restaurants and on public transport

• Prepared to take risks
• She uses technology to help her
• She is fearless when hitchhiking
• Does not give up, despite bad weather, travel difficulties
• She is very sociable / vivacious / cheerful

• She trusts her instincts

• Learns / draws lessons from her experiences
• Very mature for a 20-year old.

• She stubbornly insists on travelling alone when nobody wanted to go with her
• Takes unacceptable risks when on her own
• She sets off with no money
• She believes what she reads on blogs and trusts the accommodation website
• Steals drinks in fast-food restaurant
• She appears to eat very little
• She picks destinations at random
• She cheats on public transport
• She hitchhikes on the motorway
• She dismisses others, like Justine, who worry about her
• She takes risks with strangers
• She exploits others (Justine, the two men)
• She has said “Yes” very often
• Relies too much on her instincts.
Etc., etc.

Disagree:

• She spoils the children / buys them ice cream
• She falls asleep when she should be looking after the children
• She doesn’t see Mila going away
• She panics when Mila is not to be seen
• She scolds Mila when she finds her with the woman. Etc., etc.

Use the separate answer spaces where provided. Two or more answers on one line count as one answer. An extra subdivision is rewarded only if an earlier answer is cancelled.

Excess material: deduct 1 or 2 marks. All other errors together: deduct at most 1 mark per question or segment (inappropriate quotation, unnecessary manipulation, grammar in manipulation, required manipulation not attempted, or wrong answer language). The excess-material penalty may also apply.
Give 2 distinct points. Each earns at most 5 marks; do not score the same point twice.
answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree or disagree using the following points:
Any two of the following points:
• It’s like a small house rather than a shelter, and is comfortable, bright and warm.
• It’s open seven days a week, and can take up to sixty people.
• It’s nicely furnished, with a sofa, wooden floor, modern furniture, white walls and large windows.
• They can eat there, and even have a nice hot meal.
• They can shower, wash clothes and get clean clothes.
• They can sit on a couch, watch television, play pinball or table-football, or smoke.
• They are made to feel valued there and their freedom is respected.
• Their treatment in the centre is a contrast with the way they are ignored in the outside world.
• They are not forced to find work, or type out a CV as soon as they arrive.
• They can have a part-time job and still come to the centre.
• They are not judged, but instead are helped to find solutions for rebuilding their lives.
• There’s supervised consumption of alcohol, medical follow-up, and social workers.
• They are helped to make contact with their families.
Etc., etc.

answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree or disagree using the following points:
Any two of the following points:
• Often trains are full or too expensive and generally young people / students have no money.
• Suits young people / students as they generally have a taste for freedom, for the unknown and for risk.
• It’s back in fashion due to the Internet and hitch-hikers can get advice and tips from others online.
• It works well in France and generally a vehicle will stop after one has been waiting no more than ten or fifteen minutes.
• It can be a good experience if one takes precautions such as, like Julia, taking a moment to check out the occupants or by using GPS to be sure of where you are going.
Etc., etc.
• Sometimes hitch-hikers are not very welcome, for example at toll stations.
• They may have to wait a long time for a lift.
• The lift may not get them all the way to their destination.
• They don’t know what kind of person they are going to travel with, for instance if they smoke.
• It could be dangerous for a girl to take a lift in a car with four boys.
• Car-sharing is better in many ways.
Etc., etc.

questionText: Nathan is a cool, calculating person. Do you agree? Refer to the text in support of your answer. (Two points, about 50 words in total.)

sourceMaterial.attribution: SEC French 2011 Higher Level examination paper — © State Examinations Commission.
sourceMaterial.presentationNote: Read the original passage and return to this task. Answer in English or Irish.

schemeCitation: SEC French 2011 Higher Level marking scheme, pp.14; general rules p.3 — © State Examinations Commission.

taskRequirements: Answer in English or Irish.
Use the separate answer spaces where provided. Two or more answers on one line count as one answer. An extra subdivision is rewarded only if an earlier answer is cancelled.

Excess material: deduct 1 or 2 marks. All other errors together: deduct at most 1 mark per question or segment (inappropriate quotation, unnecessary manipulation, grammar in manipulation, required manipulation not attempted, or wrong answer language). The excess-material penalty may also apply.
Give 2 distinct points. Each earns at most 5 marks; do not score the same point twice.
answerGuide: Candidates may choose to agree or disagree using the following points:
Any two of the following points
• He decides to take advantage of Goodrich’s absence to break into the house.
• He weighs up the risks of being observed, carefully looking around him / noting neighbours are a distance away.
• He calculates the best way to get into the house, i.e. via the garage roof and balcony.
• He was fully aware that he was breaking the law, yet he carries on.
• He fully realises the consequences of being caught, i.e. losing his lawyer’s licence, but still continues.
• He knew that care and speed were essential to avoid being caught once he got into the house.
Etc., etc.
• When the dog appears he loses his cool, begins to sweat, steps back and kicks the dog.
• His frantic efforts to find what he wanted and the knocking over of the documents suggest impatience, even panic.
• He becomes completely absorbed in what he finds, unaware of the cold or of the car arriving.
• His trembling hands and fast-beating heart suggest his excited reaction to what he was reading.
Etc., etc.

guidance: Use the accepted answers and partial-credit rules above, then apply any stated deductions.
